problem_statement:
Fix #6101: omit NON_EMPTY Map when CUSTOM content filter removes all entries

Fixes #6101

### Root cause
For a `Map` property annotated `@JsonInclude(value=NON_EMPTY, content=CUSTOM, contentFilter=...)`, `MapSerializer.isEmpty()` compared the content filter (`_suppressableValue`) to the **whole `Map`** (`supp.equals(value)`) rather than to each entry value. The filter never matches the `Map` object, so the property was deemed non-empty and written; the write path then correctly filtered every entry, leaving `{"stuff":{}}` instead of omitting the property.

Both `isEmpty()` loops had this — the statically-typed value-serializer loop and the fallback loop used when the value serializer is resolved dynamically.

### Change
Compare the content filter to each entry value (`supp.equals(elemValue)`), matching the write path (`serializeFields`, which already does `suppressableValue.equals(valueElem)`) and the existing `content=NON_EMPTY` branch. This aligns with the long-standing Map behavior (#1649) of dropping a Map that becomes empty after content filtering.

### Test evidence
New regression test `JsonIncludeMapContentFilter6101Test` (in `ser/filter`), covering both the static (`Map<String,String>`) and dynamic (`Map<String,Object>`) value-serializer paths:
- the two empty-after-filter cases (`mapEmptyAfterContentFilter`, `dynamicValueMapEmptyAfterContentFilter`) **fail before / pass after** the fix;
- surviving-entry and genuinely-empty cases pass throughout.

Verification done: ran `JsonIncludeMapContentFilter6101Test` (5/5 pass with fix; the 2 empty-case tests fail without it) plus the neighbouring `JsonIncludeCustomTest`, `JsonIncludeContainerEmpty6065Test`, and `MapInclusionTest` (all green) via `./mvnw test`.
